title: policy-playback-and-slo-sim-session-ember-technologies
summary: Intro to Redwood Console's policy playback and SLO simulation features focused on org/project key segmentation. Covered traffic replay, quota templates, per-project burst lanes, and SOC2/KMS questions. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with historical traffic replay and an SLO baseline report.

Ethan Cole - share runbook for traffic replay and required log format - 2026-11-22

Aisha Khan - confirm SOC2 scoping questions and send security contact - 2026-11-21

Customer to upload 7 days of traces and mapping file
Schedule SLO simulation run and review session the week of 2026-11-30
Redwood to share SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM integration notes
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM), Sofia Ramos (CTO - Ember), Liam Park (Platform Eng), Aisha Khan (Security), Ravi Menon (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick run through of policy playback and SLO sim; talked about org/project key patterns and how to simulate burst/fairshare. action items captured.

00:00 - Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, we'll just do intros quickly — I'm Maya, account exec on Redwood, Ethan is our solutions engineer, Jordan is your CSM.
00:18 - Sofia: Hi, Sofia here, quick note we have a hard deadline for proof point by end of Q4 so hoping this is fast.
00:25 - Ethan: great, we built today to demo the console feature called policy playback and the SLO simulation tool. We'll show how it ties into org and project keys so you can test quotas and burst lanes with your real traffic.
00:41 - Liam: quick question, when you say "org key" are you talking about an auth token that maps to an org id or a different abstraction?
00:49 - Maya: yes, org key maps to the top-level tenant, project keys are child tokens — they can be scoped to teams or apps. It's how we implement per-project quotas and fairshare.
01:03 - Liam: ok that helps. we have a mix of internal and customer-facing keys so we need sticky routing so internal traffic doesn't contend with prod.
01:12 - Ethan: sticky routing and priority lanes are possible — on the console you can set priority policy that pins certain project keys to reserved capacity, or set burst tokens.
01:25 - Ravi: are burst tokens the leaky bucket style or token bucket? i want to understand credit refill.
01:31 - Ethan: token-bucket like, with configurable refill rate and max burst. You can also set fairshare windows to prevent sustained noisy neighbors.
01:39 - Aisha: for security, we need to know data residency and whether customer data touches the control plane during replay.
01:46 - Maya: good point — policy playback runs in your sandbox org, logs are optional to upload; you can anonymize traces. The control plane sees metadata for routing but payloads can stay on-prem if you use Private deployment.
02:00 - Sofia: can we run the playback against our dedicated pool? we want to validate latency tail under load.
02:06 - Ethan: yes, you can target dedicated capacity or a hosted sandbox. We'll show later how to map rules to a specific capacity pool. For latency tails we have SLO sim that replays traces and gives p50/p95/p99 estimates.
02:21 - Liam: what format for traces? we have gzipped JSON lines with timestamp, key id, model, tokens, latency.
02:29 - Ethan: perfect — we accept ndjson with those fields. We'll provide a template and small conversion script.
02:36 - Jordan: note — action item: Ethan to share runbook.

03:05 - Ethan: jumping into the console — sorry if the screen is a bit fuzzy, I am on a new VM. So this is the sandbox org, you can see the org-level policy page. Here you can add a policy and choose "playback" as an enforcement mode.
03:20 - Ethan: policy conditions include key_id, project tag, model family, region, and request meta. You can set quotas per minute/hour/day and choose enforcement behaviour: reject, queue, degrade (route to cheaper model), or throttle.
03:35 - Sofia: degrade, is that automatic or manual? like fallback model?
03:40 - Ethan: configurable: you can set a fallback model variant. For example if your high-quality 70b model is busy we can fall back to a quantized 8-bit variant automatically.
03:52 - Liam: is there an SDK flag to request preferential routing? we have client libs and would rather tag than change token rotation.
03:58 - Maya: recommend using project-scoped API key metadata and header hints; we show sample SDK code in the docs — it's a simple metadata header like X-Project-Tag.
04:10 - Ravi: the SLO sim, how exact is the latency prediction? we need to present credible numbers to execs.
04:16 - Ethan: it's a statistical estimate — we run your trace through our kernel-selection heuristics and queuing model; results include expected p50/p95/p99 and cost delta vs baseline. It's not a perfect digital twin but it's accurate for capacity planning.
04:31 - Aisha: SOC2 questions — do you do customer-managed keys?
04:35 - Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integration, bring-your-own keys, and audit logs. We'll share our SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide.
04:48 - Aisha: please send the encryption at rest details and key rotation policies.
04:52 - Maya: noted.

05:20 - Ethan: now I'll start a quick policy playback demo — I'm going to upload a small trace and show how we bin requests by project key and simulate enforcement.
05:30 - [upload noise / pause]
05:45 - Ethan: ok trace parsed — you'll see this heatmap of request volume by hour and by key. On the right we have a timeline where we can inject a quota rule.
06:00 - Ethan: I'm going to create a rule: project_key = ember-internal -> rate limit 300 rps sustained with 500 burst, enforcement = queue with max latency 500ms. And another rule: project_key = ember-frontend -> reserve 30% of capacity with fallback to quantized model after 100ms.
06:27 - Liam: can those be templated across projects? we have 40 projects.
06:31 - Ethan: yes, you can create quota templates and apply via tag selectors or folder patterns. We'll also show how to roll them out with canary.
06:40 - Maya: quick note, applying a template will show a simulated impact on cost and latency before committing.
06:48 - Sofia: what's policy playback's typical runtime? we don't want it to take days.
06:53 - Ethan: depends on trace size, but 7 days of traces for a single org typically runs in 1-3 hours in the sandbox. You can parallelize runs.
07:05 - Ravi: any chance we can run it in our VPC? we prefer private replay.
07:10 - Maya: yes with Redwood Private we can mount the replay worker in your VPC, so traces never leave your network.

07:35 - Ethan: starting the simulation now — you'll see the SLO simulator compute p95 and p99 with and without the new policy.
07:43 - Ethan: ok p95 baseline is 210ms, with policy applied p95 moves to 230ms for internal keys but frontend p95 improves from 420ms to 290ms. Cost delta is +6% due to reserved lanes.
07:58 - Liam: that tradeoff looks acceptable if frontend user latency improves. We need to experiment with smaller reserved bands to reduce cost.
08:08 - Ethan: you can run a sensitivity sweep over reserved capacity; the console supports automated sweeps and will output a csv.
08:17 - Jordan: note — customer interested in a sensitivity sweep during pilot.

08:45 - Maya: let's talk about org/project key hygiene — we often advise mapping long-lived machine keys to org admin tasks and short-lived project keys for ephemeral services to avoid cross-contamination.
08:58 - Sofia: we rotate keys nightly via our secrets manager, does that break project mappings?
09:04 - Ethan: not if you keep the mapping file, we have an API to rebind keys to projects; token rotation is expected and supported.

09:30 - Aisha: audit logs — do you produce token-level logs with anonymized payloads?
09:36 - Maya: yes, we have audit events with token id, caller IP, model used, and an optional checksum of the payload. You can toggle payload capture.
09:46 - Aisha: what about retention limits? legal asks for 7 years for some customers.
09:51 - Maya: retention is configurable for Private and Dedicated; hosted has standard tiers but enterprise add-on supports extended retention. We'll include options in the SOW.

10:20 - Ethan: now switching to API view — here's how to create a quota via API and how to call the playback endpoint. It's a multipart upload: trace file + mapping file + rule set. We'll post a gist with cURL and Python examples.
10:36 - Liam: do you support websocket streaming for heavy traces? we could stream.
10:40 - Ethan: yep we accept chunked streaming for very large archives.

11:05 - Sofia: can we simulate model fallbacks and measure quality delta? we need to show execs the degradation in output quality if we degrade to quantized model.
11:13 - Ethan: SLO sim includes a quality metric plug-in — if you can provide a small set of eval prompts we can run them across model variants and report divergence scores.
11:23 - Sofia: good, we'll prepare 200 eval prompts.

11:50 - Ravi: any considerations for multiregion traffic? our app is global.
11:55 - Ethan: you can create region-aware policies and split reserve capacity by region; policy playback can replay geo-locations if traces include region metadata.
12:05 - Liam: latency SLOs differ by region — can the sim produce region-specific p99s?
12:09 - Ethan: yes, it breaks down by region, model, and key.

12:35 - Aisha: last security note: where do keys live in logging? are they hashed?
12:40 - Maya: keys in logs are hashed; full tokens are not stored unless explicitly opted-in in a controlled S3 bucket.
12:48 - Aisha: ok, please include the hashing algorithm and HSM info in the doc.

13:10 - Maya: recap: Redwood will provision a sandbox org, Ethan will share runbook and trace template, customer will upload traces, we'll run SLO sim and sensitivity sweeps, and deliver a baseline SLO report plus recommended policy templates.
13:28 - Sofia: timeline — can you run the first sim by 2026-11-30?
13:33 - Maya: yes we'll aim for that, contingent on trace delivery.
13:38 - Jordan: i'll schedule the follow-up review for the week of Nov 30 and send a calendar invite.

13:55 - Liam: quick cost question — what about unit economics impact if we reserve too much capacity?
14:01 - Ethan: the console shows estimated cost delta; also our Optimize module will recommend quantization and batching profiles to offset reserve costs.
14:11 - Sofia: send the Optimize recommendations as part of the pilot deliverables.

14:40 - Maya: any final questions?
14:44 - Aisha: none from security beyond what's been captured.
14:46 - Ravi: none from SRE.
14:47 - Sofia: sounds good thanks.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabeled speakers and ambient pauses. Some acronyms transcribed as separate letters (K V cache instead of KV cache).
